# Overview

On 9/23 we did our final assessment of the 10K seed at Baywater and closed out this project! We checked on the PolyIC outplants and left those deployed. We also outplanted a trial set of El Nino oysters and SORMI families.      

## Final assessment 

We did the following today to assess and close out the 10K seed experiment: 

- Collected all 10K seed bags (24 bags) from the lines and brought them up to the processing facility 
- Removed oysters from each bag and counted mortalities
- Arranged oysters for a photograph to capture number of live animals and for growth analysis
- Tag and scale bar included in each photo
- Subsampled oysters from each bag to total n=~30 oysters per treatment group (5 treatment groups total) into red mesh bags with their own tag labels for survival assays in the lab (see below)
- Bags and equipment were cleaned 
- Two temperature loggers were downloaded that were brought in on the bags. There is still one logger remaining with the PolyIC outplants in the field. One logger was attached to a mesh bag to follow the oysters to UW.  
- I recorded data and uploaded size image photos.  

All data is in our [10K seed GitHub repo](https://github.com/RobertsLab/10K-seed-Cgigas/).

## Samples for survival assays

Here is a table of the tags collected today from Baywater. I will use this to help Jesse and Maddy prepare datasheets for assays. Each bag has about 30-35 oysters. 30 will be used for collections.   

See our methods plan [in my previous post here for the survival assays](https://ahuffmyer.github.io/posts/2026-09-21-fall-lab-survival-assessment-plan.html).

## PolyIC checks  

The PolyIC oysters grew a lot! We redistributed a couple of over packed bags into other bags from the same treatment group. We also pulled out bag 362 because it was open and empty.
